title: API Gateway authorizers
summary: Users call the API with a Cognito token that a JWT authorizer checks, and internal services sign their calls with IAM. API Gateway then invokes the backend Lambda under the function's resource-based policy.
notes: An HTTP API's JWT authorizer checks the token's signature against the issuer's keys, its expiry, and that the audience (or client_id for Cognito access tokens) is on the allowed list. Routes can also require scopes. REST APIs do the same job with a Cognito user pool authorizer or a Lambda authorizer.
Service-to-service routes can use IAM authorization instead. The caller signs the request with SigV4, and its role needs execute-api:Invoke on the specific API, stage, method and path.

API Gateway invokes Lambda under the function's resource-based policy, which allows the apigateway.amazonaws.com principal. Add a SourceArn condition for this API, so no other API can invoke the function.
The backend receives the checked claims in the request context, not just the raw header, so it doesn't need to validate the token again.
Usage-plan API keys are for throttling and quotas. AWS says not to use them for authentication or authorization.
